correctness.rationale: The size-two neighborhoods at b_2 and a_{n-1} force distinct same-side endpoint colors, while the nested half-graph edges force all four endpoint-core colors to be pairwise distinct. After fixing these four colors, properness leaves a binary sequence on a_1 through a_{n-1} and a reversed binary sequence on b_2 through b_n. A binary sequence beginning with distinct symbols can have a singleton in every prefix only if all positions from the third onward are constant; the dual suffix statement is identical. The last A-vertex and first B-vertex then have exactly two choices each. The converse forms satisfy both properness and every singleton-neighborhood condition. Exhaustive checks for n=4,5 match the complete 384-coloring count.

value.rationale: Half graphs are canonical nested-neighborhood bipartite graphs. The result gives not only the exact PCF chromatic number but the entire optimum space, which stabilizes at sixteen color-permutation classes and 384 named colorings for every order n at least four. The proof isolates a four-vertex forcing core and shows that the remaining vertices collapse into two binary monotone blocks, giving a reusable structural picture rather than a routine finite computation.
